Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's second innings! The Indian players stride out to the middle, followed by Rory Burns and Haseeb Hameed. Umesh Yadav will start with the ball. Burns to face. India have two substitutes as Suryakumar Yadav and Mayank Agarwal have come on for Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara. Pujara is feeling some discomfort in his left ankle, which got twisted a touch on Saturday while Sharma has an issue in his left knee.
... THE FOURTH INNINGS ...

Right then! India hold all the cards at the moment. They would hope that they can pick some wickets before Stumps on Day 4 while England would want to start well and hope not to lose many wickets before the end of the day's play. They are certainly not out of it. Join us for England's second innings in a while.

England toiled and toiled but they were put to the sword. Chris Woakes was the pick of the bowlers for them while Anderson's woes in the second innings continued. Overton had a tough time while Robinson did a decent job but they all looked tired in the middle. Moeen Ali and Joe Root were in the wickets column but one would feel that England have given few runs too many.

India started really well with the bat as Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul took England on and gave the visitors a very good start. They put up an 83-run stand before Rahul was dismissed. Then the partnership between Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara took over. Rohit Sharma scored a magnificent century while Pujara was brilliant in his knock. Kohli and Jadeja contributed but it was Pant and Thakur who took the game head-on. Thakur scored a fine 60 while Pant got back to form. There were some useful contributions from the lower order as well and India have gotten a very good lead.

End of a very good batting performance from India! They are right on top here and they will feel that it is them that hold all the cards at the moment. England, on the other hand, need to bat really well, despite the pitch being a very good one to bat on. It won't be easy for them.

England toiled hard throughout but they have been hammered by the Indians. Shardul Thakur and Rishabh Pant took them to the sword and they faltered. All the seamers looked tired from the workload but they gave it their all. It looked like it will be a wicket-less session but Root and Ali provided them the two breakthroughs. They would now look to pick up the remaining two wickets as quickly as possible. Will India declare soon or will England get them all out? Join us at 4 pm local (3 pm GMT) for the final session of Day 4.

India started well after Lunch as Shardul Thakur and Rishabh Pant kept milking the runs and once the lead went past 300, they started to attack and helped India gain momentum. Thakur reached his fifty and then fell while Pant too departed after getting back to form. One thought that the declaration might come after Pant's dismissal but India felt they could get more runs and what we are seeing is another partnership forming. Umesh Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah kept England at bay while playing some lovely shots in the middle. That stand is worth 31 and it has taken just 39 balls. One feels that post Tea, the visitors will bat for 30-45 minutes and then declare, with a probable lead of around 400. 43 overs are left in the day, so plenty of time left.

Another great session for India. They are well on top as they lead by 346 runs. They will be pleased with the effort and Virat Kohli looks a happy man in the dressing room. England look deflated and they need a big performance if they want to forget win, even save the Test from here.

England were brilliant with the ball, they have been lethal and have bowled superb lines and lengths. Chris Woakes was terrific while Robinson, Anderson and Overton were decent as well. Moeen Ali was the one who got into the wickets column on Day 4 and they would look to wrap up this innings as quickly as possible. India, on the other hand, would look for one more hour with the bat post Lunch. That should swell the lead close to 300 and put them into safe territory. The second session will begin at 1.40 pm local (12.40 pm GMT). Do join us then.

India started the day well, with Jadeja and Kohli doing a very good job. Kohli played some lovely shots but then Jadeja and Rahane fell in quick succession to put them on the back foot. The runs dried up and Kohli too departed. Pant and Thakur have kept England at bay since then but they have a job to do after the break.

A session which has belonged to England! They started the day behind but they have made a good comeback, picking up three wickets and they will be pleased. India, on the other hand, are still slightly ahead but they will be disappointed that they could not take the game by the scruff of the neck.

On a length, on off. Jadeja blocks it to point.

On a length, outside off. Kohli shoulders arms to it.
Serves a length ball, on off. Kohli prods forward to defend and does it off the inner half of his bat to square leg.

We are all set to begin Day 4! The England players stride out to the middle, followed by Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja. Ollie Robinson to start with the ball. Remember, the play will be extended by 18 minutes today and a minimum of 95 overs will be bowled.

BREAKING NEWS! There is some news coming in that 4 of India's backroom staff, including Ravi Shastri are in isolation as they returned a positive Covid Test. However, the good news is that all the Indian and English players took their respective tests and none of those returned positive. Phew.

Pitch report - Dominic Cork says that it has turned into a belting batting track and it has dried up a little. Adds that it will be very interesting to see what Day 4 brings. States that if a heavy roller is used, then the pitch might become flatter.

Rohit Sharma is up for a chat. Rohit says that he was mentally prepared for the challenge and he knew that the management had faith in him. Adds that they always have to take risks and he was ready for it and it did not come to him as a surprise. States that he wanted to get big runs and he is pleased that he was able to play 250 balls. Adds that it was his goal to play as many balls as possible and spending time in the middle is the biggest takeaway.
Breaking news - KL Rahul has been fined 15 percent of his match fees as he showed dissent when he was given out caught behind on Day 3. A demerit point has also been added to his disciplinary record.

England, on the other hand, are in trouble. If they want to make a comeback in this game, they would need to pick up wickets as quickly as possible. They have already conceded a lead of 170 but they are not out of the game yet and if they can restrict India to as low a lead as possible, they can win from here. All-in-all, an exciting day awaits us.

How much will India aim for? That is the question in one's mind right now. Anything above 300 would be a very good score and India would want that. Kohli is looking in good touch and India would hope that he, along with the rest of the batters can stick around and take India past the 300 lead. The pitch looks good for batting and India would be disappointed with anything below 300.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of the 4th Test between England and India. After a riveting Day 3, it is India who have moved ahead in the game as they lead by 171 runs and are looking good, despite losing two set batters late on Day 3. They have Kohli and Jadeja in the middle and they have plenty of batting left. England, on the other hand, are in need of wickets quickly before the lead swells up more. They have bowled well but with little reward. What will happen here?
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Over and out! India will head into Day 4 with their noses in front. They are ahead by a good margin but with six sessions still left in this Test match, the tourists are not completely out of woods. England will have a fairly new ball to work with in the morning session and they would aim to create early inroads and restrict India's lead to as low as possible. Do join us on Sunday at 11 am local (10 am GMT) for all the action. The build-up will begin much in advance. Cheers!

England were mostly on the money but managed to pick only three wickets in the day's play. Missing out on a couple of opportunities to dismiss Rohit Sharma, in the first hour of the morning session, proved to be fatal. Not many would remember but Sharma offered a run out chance when he was on 28 but Anderson failed to score the direct hit from mid on. After that, there was one more chance to catch Rohit's edge but Rory Burns once again was the culprit. Rohit Sharma went on to score his maiden Test hundred outside home and made England pay heavily.

The first session was quite challenging for the batsmen but India braved that with minimum damage as they lost only KL Rahul. Day 3 is usually considered to be the best batting day at The Oval and as expected, the conditions were ripe for batting in the afternoon and the Indian pair of Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara prospered. Their century stand pushed the hosts into a corner and they looked out of ideas. The pitch flattened out and the soft ball was not doing anything threatening.

From 99 down to 171 ahead. India have stormed back into this Test match. Apart from that one over with the second new ball when Ollie Robinson removed both Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara in quick succession, the day belonged entirely to India. If Day 3 is the 'moving day', then this Test match has moved in favour of the visitors, at least for now.
Update 6 pm local (5 pm GMT) - The light, as expected, has not improved. The umpires have decided to call for STUMPS ON DAY 3.

Moeen Ali to operate from the other end.

They have decided to continue for now, maybe on the condition that England can bowl only spin. Joe Root has agreed and has brought himself into the attack. A bit strange decision. Drinks! What a passage of play we have had here! Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara started the session well but then the second new ball changed things as Ollie Robinson sent both Sharma and Pujara packing in the same over. Kohli and Jadeja have held the fort since then and they need to continue. England would look to pick some more wickets before Stumps. An exciting final passage of play coming up.

We are all set to begin the final session of Day 3! The England players make their way out to the middle, followed by Rohit Sharma and Cheteshwar Pujara. Craig Overton will start with the ball. 7-0-27-0 are his figures so far. The field is set for some short stuff. A fly slip, a short leg, deep square leg in place. Here we go...

Right then! Post Tea, India would look to carry on batting as long as they can and get a big lead while England would want to break this partnership first and then make further inroads into the Indian batting line-up. This game has turned in the favour of India but things can change quickly in cricket. What will happen? Do join us at 3 pm GMT (4 pm local) for all the action after Tea.

England, on the other hand, had to toil hard after Lunch! James Anderson and Chris Woakes bowled well and had the Indian batters in trouble on a few occasions but they were not rewarded. Moeen Ali has looked unthreatening so far and the Indian batters have made merry off his bowling. Ollie Robinson looked tired while Craig Overton did not bowl much. Starting after Lunch, India got off to a positive start as Pujara looked really good. He played those cut shots really well and looked in sublime touch. England didn't pick too many wickets but at the same time, they didn't leak runs. Only 65 runs came in the morning and that should be their plan after Lunch as well. The good work done in the first session is a thing of the past now and they will have to switch on and start afresh. Do join us at 12.40 pm GMT (1.40 pm local) for all the action after Lunch.

India are effectively 9 for 1 at this stage and this Test match continues to hang right in the balance. Rohit Sharma is approaching his fifty and after surviving three nervy moments, he would be aiming for a big knock. His partner Cheteshwar Pujara has looked very positive in his 21-ball stay so far and his strike rate of 66.7 hints that he is looking for runs.

End of an absorbing session and India will be quite pleased with their efforts. The conditions were challenging for the batsmen but Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul braved everything together for most parts. England worked hard with the ball but their lengths were not accurate enough. They had mastered their lengths in Headingley by bowling a bit fuller but here they appeared more on the shorter side. A couple of chances also went begging in the first hour when Rohit's run out chance was missed and then Rory Burns offered Sharma yet another life. Jimmy eventually managed to eke out an edge off KL Rahul's bat and that was the only success for the Three Lions in the morning session.

Pitch report - Dominic Cork is near the surface and he starts by sharing that the weather is similar like it was on the first two days. Adds that it's overcast, chilly and a bit breezy too. Informs that currently, it's 16 degrees but the temperature is expected to rise to 22-23 degrees and it will get warmer. The Englishman mentions that to bat the whole day and put England under pressure will be the plan for India. Regarding the pitch, Cork tells that it has not changed a lot and still there is some green tinge. He spots a few rough areas also but too wide for the bowlers to use. Signs off by saying that it's going to be a massive first hour and session.

Did you know? On this day, exactly 42 years ago, Sunil Gavaskar notched up 221 runs in the 4th innings at The Oval. It was a breathtaking knock and the original Little Master almost helped India achieve a miracle win, chasing a mammoth target of 438. That game was eventually drawn with India remaining a few runs short. To date, Gavaskar's knock remains the highest score by an Indian in the fourth innings. Truly inspirational.

Ravi Shastri had mentioned recently that all the pressure is on England as this is their home Test series and India have done what they had to do when England visited them earlier this year. The Indian coach smartly played down the situation but we all know there's a burning desire for India to win a Test series in England. Day 3 of the 4th Test can drop us a hint of whether it's achievable or not.

Shardul Thakur with the bat, Umesh Yadav with the ball, Ollie Pope's knock and Chris Woakes' all-round quality - It's safe to say that this Test match belongs to the non-regulars. They've had a big impact already after two innings and let's wait and watch if the regulars get their act together for the next three days. It's always said that the Dukes ball starts to swing more after 12-15 overs in England, so a big challenge awaits India and along with that you cannot discount the early morning conditions. After what happened at Headingley, the tourists will be extra careful and seeing off Anderson and co. in the first session would be the key.

Two days, 20 wickets and some rearguard batting - That's been the story of The Oval Test thus far. We're a firm believer in momentum but currently, as we head into the 'moving day', it's hard to guess which team has it. This is what happens when two top-class teams collide who have similar strengths and weaknesses. Just because England still have a lead, we can't hand the advantage to them as the Indian openers almost halved the deficit after batting bravely in the last evening session. So, let's sit on the fence and for the moment use that cliched line - This Test is tantalizingly poised and the morning session of Day 3 holds great importance. Right then, on that note, allow us to welcome you for the coverage and stay tuned as we head towards the action.

That is it from the coverage of Day 2! It's been an engrossing day of Test cricket. The first two sessions were shared by both the sides, but the final session surely belonged to India. Can they hold the advantage on Day 3 as well? We will have to wait and find out. The first ball will be bowled at 1100 local (1000 GMT) but the buildup will begin well in advance. Do tune in early. Till then, take care and goodbye!

The openers batted solidly! Indian openers had their task cut out. They showed a lot of discipline and also scored runs at a brisk pace. Both KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma negotiated the new ball realy well and made sure that India ended the day unscathed. It will be important for them to carry on and post a good opening stand by laying a foundation for the batters to follow.

The Indian bowlers did what was asked from them, but leaked away quite a few runs in the end! India bowled well in patches in the third session as they did concede a lot of loose balls and the English batters pounced on it, especially Chris Woakes. Shardul Thakur got rid of Pope while, Jadeja dismissed Robinson in no time. Woakes stood tall and helped his side to get a very good lead of 99 runs and also got his fifty in the process. He ran out of partners and as a result had to sacrifice his wicket in the end but the damage had already been done.

What an intriguing day of Test cricket we have witnessed yet again. Both teams went hard at each other with the series on the line. England did manage to go past India's total and they managed to get a healthy lead of 99 runs. Ollie Pope and Chris Woakes starred with the bat for the hosts and kept England in the driver's seat. Moeen Ali and Jonny Bairstow also contributed to their team's total after they lost both of their overnight batters early on in the day. Indian openers did well to remain unscathed and they go back with a trail of 56 runs.
